title: Simple Elastic-Waist Skirt
summary: A gathered, pull-on skirt drafted from your own waist, hip and length.
description: Two rectangles, an elastic casing and a hem — but drafted from your measurements so it actually fits. The panel width is based on your hip (so it always pulls on), the elastic on your waist, and the length is yours to choose.

params.label: Waist
params.help: Around your natural waist, tape snug but not tight.

params.label: Hip
params.help: Around the fullest part of your hips.

params.label: Skirt length
params.help: From waist down to where you want the hem.

customNote: This pattern is drafted, not scaled: panel width comes from your hip × 1.5 fullness (minimum hip + 20 cm so it always pulls on), elastic from 90% of your waist plus a 2 cm overlap, and length from your chosen length plus fixed casing and hem allowances. Seam allowance stays 1.5 cm at every size. Size presets are typical body measurements — your own measurements are better.

materials.name: Light woven fabric
materials.why: Skirt panels — softer fabrics gather and drape better.

materials.name: Woven/knitted elastic, 3 cm wide
materials.why: Holds the skirt up. Knitted or woven elastic keeps its width when stretched.

pieces.name: Skirt panel (front & back)
pieces.notes: Front and back are identical; mark the back with a safety pin.

steps.title: Take your measurements
steps.text: Measure your waist (where you want the skirt to sit), your hip at its fullest point, and the length from your waist to where you want the hem. Enter them in 'Customise' on the project page — every piece below updates.
steps.beginner: Keep the tape level all the way round and snug, not tight. Wear thin clothing. It's easier with a helper for the length.
steps.expert: Waist, hip, length → enter in Customise.
steps.alt: A simple body outline with the waist line, fullest-hip line and skirt length marked.

steps.title: Pre-wash the fabric
steps.text: Wash and dry the fabric as you'll launder the skirt. Rayon and linen can shrink a lot — this matters for the length. Press it smooth.
steps.alt: Fabric before and after pre-washing, slightly smaller after.

steps.title: Cut the two panels
steps.text: Lay the fabric single-layer and cut two identical rectangles with the length running parallel to the selvedge. Mark the back panel with a safety pin.
steps.beginner: These are big rectangles — use the full length of a table and check your corners are square with a large ruler or the edge of a book.
warnings: Rotary cutters are very sharp: always close the guard.
steps.alt: Cutting layout with two tall skirt panels.

steps.title: Sew and finish the side seams
steps.text: Place the panels right sides together and sew both side seams with a 1.5 cm seam. Neaten each pair of edges with zigzag or overlock, or press the seams open and zigzag each edge separately.
steps.alt: Two skirt panels right sides together with both side seams stitched.

steps.title: Press and stitch the casing
steps.text: At the top edge, press 1 cm to the wrong side, then press again by the casing depth shown. Stitch close to the lower fold all the way around, leaving a 5 cm gap at one side seam for the elastic.
steps.beginner: Pressing the side-seam allowances in one direction under the casing makes threading the elastic easier.
steps.expert: Casing: 1 cm + (ew + 1) cm; stitch leaving 5 cm gap.
steps.alt: The top edge folded into a casing, stitched along its lower edge with a gap at the side.

steps.title: Cut and thread the elastic
steps.text: Cut the elastic to the length shown. Pin a safety pin to one end and feed it through the casing gap, all the way around. Pin the trailing end to the skirt so it can't slip inside.
steps.beginner: Wrap the elastic round your waist before cutting to check it's comfortable — it should be snug but not dig in.
steps.alt: Elastic being fed through the casing with a safety pin.

steps.title: Join the elastic ends
steps.text: Check the elastic isn't twisted all the way round. Overlap the ends by 2 cm and zigzag a box across the overlap. Let the elastic slip into the casing.
steps.alt: Elastic ends overlapped two centimetres and stitched with a zigzag box.

steps.title: Close the casing and set the gathers
steps.text: Stitch the casing gap closed. Spread the gathers evenly around the elastic. Stitch-in-the-ditch through the casing and elastic at each side seam so the elastic can't roll or twist.
steps.expert: Close gap; distribute gathers; tack elastic at side seams.
steps.alt: The gathered waistband with a vertical tack stitch at the side seam.

steps.title: Try on and press the hem
steps.text: Try the skirt on and check the length. Press 1 cm to the wrong side at the hem, then 3 cm more. Pin.
steps.beginner: If you want it shorter, trim the extra off the hem edge first — keep the 4 cm allowance below your new hemline.
steps.alt: The hem folded up and pinned on the wrong side.

steps.title: Stitch the hem
steps.text: Stitch the hem from the wrong side, close to the inner fold, all the way around. Overlap the first stitches by 2 cm.
steps.alt: Stitching along the inner fold of the hem.

steps.title: Final press
steps.text: Press the hem and side seams. Steam the gathers lightly from the right side without flattening them.

review.note: Drafting rules follow common rectangle-skirt practice; size presets are typical and not graded from a block. Not yet test-sewn.
